claims.summary: For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2, l_1 the Leighton-Shor scale, kappa > 0 fixed and s_0 = kappa sqrt(log N/N), with probability tending to one and L depending only on kappa, for every dyadic delta_0 with s_0 <= delta_0 <= 2^(-l_1): (a) every union A of cells of side delta_0 has |#(X in A) - N area(A)| <= L sqrt N (log N)^(3/4) P(A), P(A) the length of the inner grid edges separating A from its complement; (b) every g constant on the cells has |sum_i g(X_i) - N int g| <= L sqrt N (log N)^(3/4) TV(g), TV(g) = sum over inner edges of delta_0 |jump|; (c) at (4,4), if every increment |jump|/delta_0 is 0 or at least y >= 2e^16 and sum_e delta_0^2 psi*_4(|jump|/(2 delta_0)) <= 2, then TV(g) <= 8 (log(y/2))^(-1/4), so for y >= N^c the discrepancy is at most 8 3^(1/4) c^(-1/4) L sqrt(N log N).
claims.assessment: Working proof: lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (b), (c) at the Leighton-Shor mesh for the coarse averages of 1_A, whose inner variation is at most P(A) by a global Fubini count; Chernoff for the coarse counts; Bernstein conditionally on the coarse counts with a union over the subsets of the at most (4/kappa^2) sqrt(log N) fine cells of each coarse cell, at most P(A)/delta_0 cut cells; the layer-cake formula; the recorded lower bound of psi*_4.
claims.rationale: Extends the Leighton-Shor bound below its mesh to all unions of fine cells on dyadic grids; for the X-term of the discrete class split by increment level it bounds the levels from N^c on at the conjectured order and locates the obstacle at levels with log y = o(log N).
claims.next_action: A band-confined layer bound for nested layers {g>t} at spacing delta_0 in the discrete class, the fine-grid analogue of band-family (b), starting with the transfer of the band-family bound to cell averages, for a staircase along curved graphs at level (log N)^2.

relationships: Parts (b) and (c) at the Leighton-Shor mesh bound the coarse averages.

Works in the discrete class that entry reduced the smeared X-term to; for the X-term split by increment level it bounds the levels from N^c on, while the pyramids act against Lebesgue measure from levels of order (log N)^2.
